title: She Recognised Audrey Hepburn at the Door. She Said Nothing.
title_alternatives: She Recognised Audrey Hepburn at the Door. She Said Nothing.
They Were in the Same Class in 1944. Only One of Them Knew.
She Had 1.5 Seconds to Decide, and Kept to It for 11 Years
The Housekeeper Could Have Mentioned Arnhem. She Never Did.
A Job Interview in 1979, and the Thing That Was Never Said
description:
On a Thursday morning in April 1979, a woman of sixty took two buses and walked eleven minutes uphill to a house above a lake in Switzerland, to be interviewed for a position as housekeeper. She was forty minutes early, so she walked up and down a lane out of sight of the gate, because arriving early is as rude as arriving late.

The door was opened by the woman who had placed the advertisement. Marta Brouwer recognised her within about a second and a half, understood in the second after that exactly where from, and made a decision in the second after that which she kept to for the next eleven years.

The decision was to say nothing about it. Not to lie — simply not to raise it.

What gave it away was not the face. It was a particular way of standing with the weight on one hip and the other foot turned slightly out, which is trained into dancers before they are twelve and stays in the body for life, and which Marta had watched every Tuesday and Thursday afternoon in a cold room in Arnhem in 1943 and 1944, from the back row, where the girls who were not any good stood.

Twice in the fifty minutes the conversation came close to it. Once the woman mentioned having spent part of the war in Holland. Once she did some arithmetic out loud and arrived at the right year, and said it aloud, and moved on without any change in her voice at all.

Marta was never able to decide whether that had been a coincidence or an invitation, and she decided quite deliberately not to find out.

Her reason, when she finally explained it in 1994, was not modesty, and she was impatient with the suggestion.

This story is a work of fiction. Marta, the interview, the references and every detail in it are invented, created for storytelling and not drawn from any record.
